subQuestions.questionText:
The core function of management in a business is to …
A. encourage new ideas so that productivity increases.
B. guide employees in becoming active participants in the workplace.
C. be inspirational in their approach towards work.
D. administer plans and tasks to reach set targets.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
The core function of management is to administer plans and tasks to reach set targets. Options A, B and C describe leadership qualities rather than the core management function.

options.A: encourage new ideas so that productivity increases.
options.B: guide employees in becoming active participants in the workplace.
options.C: be inspirational in their approach towards work.
options.D: administer plans and tasks to reach set targets.

subQuestions.questionText:
Rozette invested an amount of R40 000 in a fixed deposit at 10% compound interest per annum for two years with Maropeng Bank. Rozette will receive … as interest after two years.
A. R48 000
B. R8 400
C. R48 400
D. R8 000
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Using compound interest: $A = P(1 + i)^n = 40\,000(1.10)^2 = 40\,000 \times 1.21 = R48\,400$. The interest portion = $R48\,400 - R40\,000 = R8\,400$.

subQuestions.questionText:
Businesses that promote social rights in the workplace …

B. pay employees equally for work of equal value.
C. allow employees to participate in legal strikes.
D. provide employees with reasonable working hours.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Providing training opportunities relates to social rights (development and access to skills). Equal pay relates to economic rights, strikes to political/labour rights and reasonable working hours to economic rights.

options.B: pay employees equally for work of equal value.
options.C: allow employees to participate in legal strikes.
options.D: provide employees with reasonable working hours.

subQuestions.questionText:

Aggressive employees are best handled by giving them space and time to speak so as not to escalate hostility toward other employees.

subQuestions.questionText: Complete the statement using the word(s) provided in the list: Silverton Manufacturing uses energy-efficient production methods. This refers to the … as a triple bottom-line element.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss any TWO stages of team development.
subQuestions.memoText:
Two stages of team development (mark first TWO only; each stage = 2 marks for naming + 1 mark per discussion point; submax 3 per stage; max 6):

Forming √√
- Individuals gather information and impressions about each other and the task √.
- Teams are comfortable and polite during this stage √.
- Focus on routines/administrative details such as organisation, who does what and when to meet √.

Storming √√
- Teams go through a period of unease/conflict after formation √.
- Different ideas compete for consideration √.
- Members open up and confront each other's ideas √.
- Tension/struggle/arguments occur √ / there may be power struggles for leadership √.
- Storming may resolve quickly or never end; many teams fail at this stage √.
- This phase can become destructive if uncontrolled √.
- This stage is necessary for growth √.
- Some members tolerate each other to survive √.

Norming √√
- Conflict from storming must be resolved to reach norming √.
- Members reach agreement and consensus √.
- Roles and responsibilities are clear and accepted √.
- Working style and respect develop √.
- Members are committed to working collectively √.
- Conflict may occur, but commitment and unity remain strong √.

Performing √√
- Members are aware of strategies and aims √.
- They have direction without leader interference √.
- Processes/structures set to achieve shared goals √.
- Leaders delegate and oversee √.
- All members are competent, autonomous and decision-capable √.
- Differences are appreciated and used to enhance performance √.

Adjourning/Mourning √√
- Focus on completion of the task/ending the project √.
- Breaking up may be traumatic as members find it hard to perform individually √.
- All tasks must be completed before the team dissolves √.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Outline the difference between limited liability and unlimited liability.
subQuestions.memoText:
Difference between limited and unlimited liability (2 marks each side, max 4; table not required; differences need not link but must be clear; max 2 if difference is unclear):

Limited liability:
- Losses are limited to the amount the owner invested in the business.
- Owner's personal assets are protected against business debts.
- Applicable to companies that have a separate legal entity/personality.

Unlimited liability:
- Liability of the owner to pay debts/claims is not limited to the business.
- Owner's personal assets may be seized to pay business debts.
- Applicable to sole proprietorships and partnerships (no separate legal entity).
[Max 4 marks]

- The partnership does not pay income tax √ — only the partners in their personal capacity √.

- Partners have unlimited liability √ and are jointly and severally liable for debts √.
- Diversity/specialisation/different skills √ can be utilised √.

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest ways in which businesses can deal with difficult employees in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Ways to deal with difficult employees (2 marks each, max 4):
- Get perspective from others who have experienced similar situations to understand difficult employees.
- Act proactively — staff problems are part of a manager's responsibility.
- Hold regular meetings with supervisors/heads to identify problem behaviour.
- Ask someone in authority for input.
- Identify the personality type causing the problem.
- Meet privately with difficult employees to avoid distractions.
- Make intentions and reasons for action known so the employee feels at ease.
- Tell employees which specific behaviours are unacceptable and allow them to explain.
- Set a deadline for improving bad behaviour.
- Discuss the deadline with the employee and monitor progress.
- Provide guidelines for improvement.
- Don't judge the person — try to understand them.
- Keep communication channels open and encourage grievance reporting.
- Build rapport by re-establishing personal connections.
- Be supportive — help difficult employees be realistic about the task.
- Remain calm and in control to encourage cooperation.
- Treat people with respect regardless of capability.
- Sometimes ignore and only monitor the difficult person.
- Take a step back and analyse before responding.
- Identify and provide an appropriate support programme to address weaknesses.
[Max 4 marks]

questions.title: SECTION C – QUESTION 5: BUSINESS VENTURES (Investment: Securities) – Essay

subQuestions.questionText:
The Johannesburg Securities Exchange (JSE) provides different financial prospects to investors. Investors must have a comprehensive understanding of the different types of investment opportunities and their risk factors. Government/RSA Retail Savings Bonds is one of the most preferred forms of investment; however, some investors also invest in preference shares.

Write an essay on investment securities in which you include the following aspects:
• Outline the functions of the Johannesburg Securities Exchange (JSE).
• Explain the following types of investment opportunities and their risk factors:
  o Debentures
  o Venture capital
• Discuss the impact of Government/RSA Retail Savings Bonds as a form of investment.
• Advise businesses on the rights of preference shareholders.
subQuestions.memoText:
ESSAY MARK BREAKDOWN: Content 32 + Insight 8 = 40

INTRODUCTION (max 2 marks; any 2 x 1):
- The JSE plays an important role in the SA economy by providing a regulated platform for trading financial securities.
- Debentures are debt securities companies issue to raise capital.
- Venture capital is a form of private equity that investors provide to small businesses with long-term growth potential.
- Government/RSA Retail Savings Bonds is a savings solution offered to citizens.
- Rights of preference shareholders protect investor interests in dividend payouts and insolvency.

FUNCTIONS OF THE JSE (max 12; 2 marks each):
- Provides opportunities for institutions (e.g. insurers) to invest surplus funds in shares.
- Serves as a barometer/indicator of SA economic conditions.
- Keeps investors informed by publishing share prices daily.
- Acts as a link between investors and public companies.
- Shares are valued and assessed by experts.
- Invites small investors to take part in the economy via buying/selling shares.
- Makes the venture capital market possible on the open market.
- Strict investment rules ensure a disciplined/orderly market.
- Raises primary capital by encouraging new investments in listed companies.
- Mobilises funds of insurance companies and other institutions.
- Regulates the market for trading shares.
- Plans, researches and advises on investment possibilities.
- Ensures the market operates transparently.
- Provides protection for investors via rules/legislation.
- Encourages short-term investment as shares can be sold any time.
- Facilitates electronic trading via STRATE / channels resources into productive activities.
- Enhances job creation and economic growth/development.

INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITIES AND RISKS (max 12; max 4 per type explanation + max 2 per risk):

Debentures (submax 4)
- Issued to raise borrowed capital √ from the public √.
- Lender/debenture holder agrees to lend money √ on certain conditions for a certain period √.
- Holders are creditors as the company is liable √ to repay the amount √.
- Most debentures can be traded √ on the JSE √.
- Holders receive annual interest payments √ based on terms held √.
Risk (submax 2)
- Low risk √ as they need to be paid back √.
- Companies must repay amount plus interest √ — decreases investor risk √.
- Investors earn a steady income via interest √ while preserving principal √.

Venture capital (submax 4)
- Given by investors to start up/expand a business √ in return for a share in the business √.
- Investors should know the type of business/markets/economic conditions √ before investing √.
- Buying a franchise/existing business succeeds √ if proper research has been done √.
Risk (submax 2)
- High risk √ if research is not properly done √.
- Inexperienced owners making wrong decisions √ may experience big losses/closure √.

IMPACT OF GOVERNMENT/RSA RETAIL SAVINGS BONDS (max 14; 2 marks each):

Positives/Advantages
- Guaranteed returns √ as the interest rate is fixed √.
- Market-related interest rates √ attract more investors √.
- Interest received twice a year √ — viable investment option √.
- Easily accessible √ — cash withdrawable after the first 12 months √.
- Low-risk/safe √ — backed by government, cannot be liquidated √.
- Affordable √ for all income levels including pensioners √.
- Easily obtained electronically √ from any Post Office/National Treasury √.
- No charges/costs/commissions √ payable on this investment √.
- Interest is usually higher √ than on fixed deposits √.
- Listed √ on capital bond markets/JSE √.
- Minors may invest with a guardian √ — encourages saving from a young age √.

AND/OR Negatives/Disadvantages
- Cannot be ceded to banks √ as security for loans √.
- Minimum R1 000/R500 √ may be hard for small investors to accumulate √.
- Not freely transferable √ amongst investors √.
- Need valid SA ID/over 18 √ — may discourage foreigners/youth √.
- Penalties for early withdrawals √ if savings is less than 12 months √.

RIGHTS OF PREFERENCE SHAREHOLDERS (max 8; 2 marks each):
- Receive dividends regardless of profits made.
- Receive a fixed rate of return/dividend.
- Are paid first / enjoy preferential rights to dividends before ordinary shareholders.
- Have a preferred claim on company assets in the event of bankruptcy/liquidation.
- Receive interim and annual reports / full financial disclosure.
- Have voting rights at the AGM only under certain circumstances/resolutions affecting their rights.
- Cumulative preference shareholders must receive outstanding/accrued dividends from previous years.
- Participating preference shareholders share in surplus profits.

CONCLUSION (max 2; any 1 x 2):
- The JSE serves as a cornerstone of SA's financial market and allows economic growth.
- Businesses benefit from issuing debentures: payment of interest is fixed and they don't share profit with debenture holders.
- Venture capital firms can also provide active support in legal/personnel matters.
- RSA Retail Savings Bonds promote national savings across financial backgrounds.
- Preference shareholders' financial interests are protected on dividends and asset claims.

INSIGHT (8 marks): Layout (2), Analysis/Interpretation (2), Synthesis (2), Originality/Examples (2). LASO – allocate 2 if all met, 1 if some met, 0 if none met.

TOTAL: 32 (content) + 8 (insight) = 40
subQuestions.topic: Investment: Securities – JSE, Debentures, Venture Capital, Retail Bonds, Preference Shares

questions.title: SECTION C – QUESTION 6: BUSINESS ROLES (Ethics and Professionalism) – Essay

subQuestions.questionText:
Businesses have a responsibility to conduct their business activities ethically and professionally by following the King Code principles for good corporate governance. They are required to understand how the various unethical business practices pose challenges to businesses. Businesses are also obligated to conduct their business practices in a professional, responsible, ethical and effective manner.

Write an essay on ethics and professionalism in which you include the following aspects:
• Outline the differences between ethical behaviour and professional behaviour.
• Explain how businesses can apply the following King Code principles of good corporate governance to improve ethical business conduct:
  o Transparency
  o Accountability
• Discuss how the THREE types of unethical business practices pose challenges to businesses.
• Suggest ways in which professional, responsible, ethical and effective business practices should be conducted.
subQuestions.memoText:
ESSAY MARK BREAKDOWN: Content 32 + Insight 8 = 40

INTRODUCTION (max 2; any 2 x 1):
- Professional and ethical behaviour are closely related concepts businesses need to uphold.
- Businesses should apply transparency and accountability as King Code principles by setting a code for ethical/professional business practices.
- Unethical business behaviour challenges moral principles, harming others and undermining trust.
- Professional, responsible, ethical and effective business practice ensures good corporate governance.

DIFFERENCES BETWEEN ETHICAL AND PROFESSIONAL BEHAVIOUR (max 8; 2 marks each side, submax 4 per side; table not required; max 4 if differences not clear):

Ethical behaviour:
- Refers to principles of right and wrong/acceptable in society.
- Conforms to a set of values that are morally acceptable.
- Forms part of a code of conduct guiding employees to act ethically.
- Focuses on developing a moral compass for decision making.
- Involves following the principles of right or wrong in business activities/practices/dealings.

Professional behaviour:
- Refers/clarifies what is right/wrong/acceptable in the business.
- Set of standards/specific level of competence of expected behaviour.
- Applying a code of conduct of a profession or business.
- Focuses on upholding the reputation of a business/profession.
- Provides guidelines on appearance/communication/attitude/responsibility.

KING CODE PRINCIPLES (max 12 total):

6.3.1 Transparency (submax 6; 1 mark per √)
- Decisions/actions must be clear √ to all stakeholders √.
- Staffing and other processes should be open √ and transparent √.
- Employees/shareholders/directors should be aware √ of employment policies √.
- Auditing reports must be accurate/available √ to stakeholders √.
- Regular audits to determine √ effectiveness √.
- Business deals conducted openly √ — no hint of dishonesty √.
- Shareholders given details of voting rights √ before/at the AGM √.
- Board reports on negative and positive impacts √ on community/environment √.
- Board ensures company ethics on information √ are reliable and effectively implemented √.

6.3.2 Accountability (submax 6; 1 mark per √)
- Regular communication √ between management and stakeholders √.
- Appoint internal and external auditors √ to audit financial statements √.
- Board ensures ethics on disclosures √ are accurate and effectively implemented √.
- Businesses should be accountable/responsible √ for decisions/actions √.
- Present accurate annual reports √ to shareholders at the AGM √.
- Top management ensures other levels are clear √ about roles and responsibilities √.

TYPES OF UNETHICAL BUSINESS PRACTICES (max 14; 3 types; submax 6 each: 2 for type + 4 for discussion; mark first THREE only):

6.4.1 Unfair advertising √√
- Unfair ads could be harmful √ to consumers √.
- Deceptive advertising violates trust √ and destroys business relationships √.
- False/misleading statements lead to misrepresentation √ negatively affecting consumers √.
- Businesses make unwise advertising choices √ under profit pressure √.
- Some ads regarded as discriminatory √ excluding/targeting sections of the population √.

6.4.2 Pricing of goods in rural areas √√
- Some rural businesses exploit customers √ by inflating prices √.
- Rural consumers have little economic power √ and are vulnerable to exploitation √.
- Monopolies in rural areas √ unilaterally raise prices √.
- Common practice to pay higher prices √ for inferior-quality goods √.

6.4.3 Taxation/Tax evasion √√
- Heavy fines √ for evading tax √.
- Tax evasion negatively impacts √ business image √.
- Accountants charged high fees √ for falsifying statements √.
- Loss of key stakeholders √ if reported √.
- Fraudulent returns to SARS √ result in penalties √.
- Businesses may not be familiar with the latest changes √ in tax legislation √.

WAYS TO CONDUCT PROFESSIONAL, RESPONSIBLE, ETHICAL AND EFFECTIVE BUSINESS PRACTICES (max 12; 2 marks each):
- Mission statement should include values of equality/respect.
- Develop equity programmes/strategies so all are treated equally regardless of rank.
- Treat workers with respect/dignity, recognising work well done.
- Plan properly with preventative measures.
- Pay fair wages/salaries in line with BCEA / remunerate for overtime/public holidays.
- Engage in environmental awareness / refrain from pollution.
- Refrain from starting a venture using ideas protected by law.
- Decisions and actions clear/transparent to all stakeholders.
- Be accountable/responsible for decisions, actions and patent rights.
- Hire honest accountants/financial officers with good credentials.
- Regular/timeous payment of taxes.
- All workers given equal opportunities/positions/resources.
- Ensure a work environment that is safe/fair/free of embarrassment.
- Comply with legislation on equal opportunities/human rights.
- Training/policies should include diversity/discrimination/harassment.
- Respond swiftly and fairly to reported discrimination.
- Orders/tasks given respectfully, allowing input.
- Draw up a code of ethics/conduct.
- Ongoing development and training for all employees.
- Performance management systems/appraisals in place.
- Adequate internal controls/monitoring/evaluation.

CONCLUSION (max 2; any 1 x 2):
- Unethical and unprofessional practices can be eliminated by implementing a code of ethics.
- Businesses applying King Code principles have a good public image and attract investors.
- Awareness of challenges enables precautionary measures to prevent negative publicity.
- Businesses must continuously research and develop ethical practice strategies.

INSIGHT (8 marks): Layout (2), Analysis/Interpretation (2), Synthesis (2), Originality/Examples (2). LASO – allocate 2 if all met, 1 if some met, 0 if none met.

TOTAL: 32 (content) + 8 (insight) = 40
subQuestions.topic: Ethics and Professionalism / King Code / Corporate Governance
